summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia in remission following double cord blood transplant, was admitted with severe diffuse joint pain and painful, infected toes. He had recently been hospitalized for Stenotrophomonas bacteremia and incomplete antibiotic treatment due to renal issues. On admission, he was found to have MRSA infection in his left big toe, which was treated with IV vancomycin and excisional debridement. His severe arthralgias, unresponsive to prior therapies, resolved completely after increasing his prednisone dose, supporting a diagnosis of graft-versus-host disease. Renal function improved with supportive care, and hyperkalemia resolved with Kayexelate. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. He was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for tapering steroids, continued vancomycin, and follow-up with transplant and podiatry teams.
